title: The Concept of Social Capital
text:
Social capital refers to the value derived from social networks and trust within a community. It encompasses the collective resources, knowledge, and mutual support that can be accessed through relationships rather than simply owned individually.

Academic study suggests that high levels of social capital—such as strong neighborhood ties or institutional trust—can buffer against economic shocks and promote civic engagement. These communal bonds facilitate cooperation and decision-making processes within a society.

Furthermore, the maintenance of social capital requires active participation and reciprocal giving; it is not a static commodity but an ongoing process reinforced by shared norms and interactions.
